title: Agent hub <-> adapter contract (agent-bus protocol)
transport: stdin/stdout, one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per LF-terminated UTF-8 line

manifest.file: plugins/<id>/manifest.json — a plugin is a directory; the directory name is its id

fields.id: must equal the plugin directory name; a manifest that claims another id is refused
fields.protocol: the adapter protocol this plugin speaks; must equal this file's version, or the hub refuses to start the adapter (harness_invalid)
fields.command: argv that starts the adapter; relative paths resolve against the plugin directory
fields.runtime: {package, version, command}: the harness this plugin drives. This is where the harness version lives — there is no separate `pin`: a version kept in two fields is a version that will one day disagree with itself, and this one did. The PLUGIN materialises the package at that version, through the `runtime` capability's `runtime/prepare` method; the hub asks for that and verifies the result, and hands `command` (absolute) to the adapter as AGENT_HUB_RUNTIME_COMMAND. Absent = the adapter brings its own runtime
fields.extensions: harness-side extensions this plugin ships (registry defaults)
fields.capabilities: what the hub may ask this plugin for; every value has an entry in capabilitySurface, and declaring one binds the plugin to its methods
fields.name: display name for the harness; falls back to the id
fields.icons: {light, dark}: the harness's own mark, each a file path relative to the plugin directory (e.g. logo.svg). `light` is the LIGHT-COLOURED mark (drawn on a dark background) and `dark` is the DARK-COLOURED mark (drawn on a light background) - the key names the mark's colour, not the theme it is shown in. The hub serves those bytes under the mark's real content type on its icon route, so a client draws the plugin's asset without reaching the disk or importing adapter code. A plugin that ships no mark omits this field and is drawn without one. Both keys are optional; a missing one falls back to the other.
fields.base: the adapter base id a consumer groups by; falls back to the id
fields.version: the harness version as the plugin declares it (not the runtime pin: see runtime.version)
fields.permissionModel: how the harness gates tools: native|extension|none — reported, never guessed
fields.planMode: how the harness carries plan mode; reported, never guessed
fields.repair: whether the harness can repair an orphaned tail; reported, never guessed
fields.provider: {apiVersion, descriptor}: this plugin ships a model-provider TYPE as DATA. The descriptor states the type's id, version, owner:'hub', display name, authMethods, configuration fields and the CATALOG SHAPE (the dialect). It is data the hub reads and maps; the hub does NOT import or run plugin code in-process (ARCHITECTURE §5). The hub owns the HTTP request, the auth, the catalog fetch and the field mapping; auth is a declared method (device-code/browser), not a plugin function. A provider-only plugin declares no command/protocol. Nothing is built in: with no plugin for a type, a provider record naming it stays readable but unusable.
fields.pluginType: what this plugin is, from a fixed set: `harness-adapter` (drives a harness; declares command/protocol) or `model-provider` ( ships a model-provider TYPE as data; declares provider). The hub uses it as the plugin's own type - a harness-adapter and a model-provider may share an id, because they are different things. Also the repo prefix: agent-hub-<kind>-<id>.
fields.summary: one line saying what this plugin is, shown in a catalog row. Metadata: it travels with every listing.
fields.release: {repository, ...}: where this plugin is published. Present in the plugin's own repo; the catalog is derived from it.

manifest.rule: a field set that does not match this list stops the hub at startup (boot self-check), it is not a warning
manifest.kindRule: id plus at least one of: command+protocol (harness adapter) or provider (a model-provider type as data). A manifest that declares neither, or a provider block whose descriptor cannot be honoured, stops the hub at startup.

requests.note: config is the preset shape (v1 defs.preset: name/persona/tools/approval/sandbox/mcp/model/context) plus materialization blocks: connections [{id,name,scheme,endpoint,envName}] (enabled only; NO credential value — a connection's token reaches the adapter as an env var named envName, injected at process start, so it never lands in this payload or in conversation history). Skills are NOT in this payload: the hub installs them into a directory the adapter is pointed at (see capabilitySurface.skills), so there is one source of truth for what is installed. core never interprets these — the adapter translates to its native dialect (A-4). MUST be called before first prompt; may be re-sent mid-session; failure = run fails, never silent fallback
the roster a caller chooses a presetId from; opaque ids, whatever names the harness uses

The hub spawns the CHILD's process and hands it where to branch from: `from` is the source session's native ref. This process opens the source only to fork it, then ADOPTS the result as its own session and answers with that ref — it is the child, not the source. The source session, its log and its live process are not touched. throughTurn is 1-based over the source's COMPLETED turns; absent = the whole conversation. The anchor is a turn because it is the only cut every harness makes exactly (pi forks before a message, so 'end with turn N' is the message that STARTS turn N+1, and the last turn is a copy; dsh snaps to the end of the turn containing its seq, and a seq past the log is a copy). A harness that cannot fork does not declare the `fork` capability and the hub answers `unsupported`.
requests.rule: never run on the source's own process: pi's fork rebinds whichever process executes it, so a source process would silently become a different conversation than the hub believes it serves (verified: the source file's hash and its live process are unaffected when another process forks)

requests.note: What the harness itself reports about this session: token totals (with cache and reasoning where it has them), cost, and context-window occupancy {tokens, window, percent}. A field the harness does not report is ABSENT — never zero, never a value computed against a window nobody declared. Read-only: it must not start, resume or change a turn.

requests.result: { compacted, reason?, tokensBefore?, tokensAfter?, summary?, usage?, detail? }
requests.note: Ask the harness to compact its own conversation. The numbers are the harness's: pi reports tokensBefore plus ITS OWN ESTIMATE of the rebuilt context (estimatedTokensAfter), and its usage for the summarization call; dsh reports the token count of the span it replaced (shadowedTokenCount) and its own context projection read right after the rewrite as tokensAfter — the same number GET /stats reports. A harness with nothing worth compacting answers compacted:false with its own words in detail ('Nothing to compact (session too small)' / 'No compactable history yet.') — that is not an error. A compaction that FAILED is an error (compact_failed).

Name the session in the harness itself, and answer with the title the harness ACCEPTED — not the one that was asked for. dsh normalizes and sanitises a title and refuses one that normalises to empty; pi appends a session_info entry, so its accepted name is read back from get_state. A title the harness did not accept is an error, never a hub-only rename that looks applied.

What THIS harness actually has, read from the harness itself — pi/jouzu from get_commands (skill:<name> entries), dsh from its skill.list RPC. It is a READ-BACK, not an echo: dsh SILENTLY drops a skill whose name is not kebab-case, whose description is missing, whose invocation keys are camelCase, or that is not a single-level bundle, and only the harness knows it did. A caller must be able to see 'installed: 4, the harness sees: 3'. The call can be slow the FIRST time on a harness that finishes its own startup lazily (jouzu measured 9s and 70s, then 24ms); the hub bounds it and reports known:false rather than an empty catalogue when it does not arrive.

Materialise the runtime this plugin's manifest pins (runtime.package + runtime.version) into <plugin>/runtime, the directory the manifest's command is relative to, and answer with what happened. Idempotent: a runtime already on disk answers ready:true and detail 'already present'. It belongs to the adapter because HOW a harness is fetched is knowledge about that harness — the hub asks, waits, and then VERIFIES the declared command exists (it installs no harness and knows no package names). Declared only by a plugin that declares the `runtime` capability; the hub calls it before session/start when the target is missing, and from POST /v1/hub/plugins/{id}/prepare.

For history-readonly adapters. Read native persisted history via a one-shot adapter without session/start, credentials/grant or config/set. No provider calls or runtime startup. Same ids/content/pagination as history/page. ref supplied only by hub session record.

events.note: the harness changed plan mode on its own (a model leaving plan when its plan is approved). The hub follows the harness: it records the flip and streams plan.changed, rather than believing its own last request

the adapter cancelled a harness dialog nobody rendered, so the agent does not hang waiting for a window that is not there. The hub drops it deliberately (no consumer yet) — declared, so the vocabulary is complete and the drop is a decision on the record

events.field: reason?: string (the harness's own word: manual|threshold|overflow on pi; manual|auto on dsh)
events.note: the harness began compacting, whether the hub asked or the harness decided (a full context compacts by itself mid-turn). Emitted so a UI can say what is happening instead of going quiet.

events.field: reason?, tokensBefore?, tokensAfter?, summary?, aborted?, willRetry?
events.note: the harness finished compacting. Sent for EVERY compaction the adapter observes, including the automatic ones nobody asked for — the same numbers the request would return.

the harness's session title changed without the hub asking — dsh titles a session by itself from the first user message (its title service is part of its own composition), and a harness UI can rename one. The hub follows the harness: it records what the harness now holds and streams session.renamed, exactly as it does for plan mode
Native non-model notification; info|warning|error; never converted into assistant text.

approval.timeoutBehaviour: No default deadline. Explicit operator timeout is fail-closed; human wait pauses session/prompt execution budget.
approval.context: Optional params.tool names the actual tool; params.args is structured review context passed unchanged into /v1 approval.args. Legacy params.detail remains supported. Context describes proposed work, not executed results.

question.timeoutBehaviour: cancel the waiting question; the harness unblocks and the model is told no answer came
question.note: Separate from approval on purpose. An approval permits one action (approved:boolean); a question asks for an answer (one entry per asked question, each {id, selected[], custom?}). An adapter MUST NOT carry a question on approval_need, nor an approval on question_need

identityRules: assistant message ids are adapter-native; never fabricated by core
user message id == clientMessageId persisted by adapter
history/page is the read-through source of truth; ids and text stable across restart+resume

requests.rule: may have network side-effects; never persists

answers what THIS harness can run: its own catalog plus the core-managed providers passed in (each {id,url,declarations}), so one query is enough. An injected provider is named `hub-<id>` in every harness. Empty catalog separated from read failure; one failure never pollutes another. Each model’s `thinkingLevels` is the list its configuration states, passed on verbatim (absent = nothing stated).

newInThisSlice.rule: partial:true when catalog incomplete; never fake completeness

invariants: session retains harness identity; core-managed provider and model may change between turns through credentials/grant then config/set; native ref is preserved
harness change requires a new session; provider change does not
unknown session id -> unknown-session; never silently creates
credential values never written to disk in plaintext by hub-managed paths
unsupported capability = explicit 'not supported' in UI, never silent fallback to another harness
disabledTools is a preset field (preset.tools.disabledTools), not a separate system; it is delivered via adapter config/set and is mutable mid-session
preset.tools honesty: never claim a block that did not happen; never silently drop a tool
Connection is a managed object: enable/disable/delete only; disable == cut-off == zero materialization

session/abort acknowledges only that the harness was ASKED to stop; the turn's own turn_end proves it stopped. An abort that could not be delivered -> error data.code='abort-failed'; an abort delivered but never confirmed is the core's cancel timeout to report, not the adapter's to hide

config/set with connectionId reports applied.modelProviderId as the requested provider identity and applied.connectionId as its resolved native route; model is selected within that route, not by bare-ID first match

Harness Adapter and Model Provider are two identities: a harness provides the agent runtime, a provider provides models. They are never conflated in names or DTOs (a session displays `via <harness> · <provider> · <model>`).

saved != validated: a successful connections/save or provider PATCH means stored, nothing more. "Usable" is a separate answer (connections/validate, or the first real request), and it is never rendered as validated before that.

capabilitySurface.note: A capability is a promise about methods AND about a hub-side surface. `methods` are the requests the plugin must answer; `hub` is the route a consumer reaches them through (null = the capability is carried inside session/start|config/set and has no route of its own).

tools.rule: known:false while no plugin declares this capability — an empty catalog is never faked

plan.carried: config/set {plan}; the harness may flip it on its own and report plan_changed

approvals.carried: the adapter initiates approval_need; the decision comes back as its reply

providers.note: routed by the hub, capability-gated (a harness without `providers` answers unsupported). Secret values a caller submits pass through to the adapter once and are stored by the harness itself (dsh: $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; jouzu: its own agent auth store); the hub keeps no copy. auth/* is forwarded verbatim and is a real implementation where the harness has one: jouzu runs its native Shisa device-code sign-in (operation state tracked by a detached runner under the harness data dir, so it outlives the one-shot config-plane process), while deepseek implements api-key only and answers unsupported-for-provider rather than faking a device flow.

skills.note: The hub INSTALLS a harness's skills before its process starts (exactly like extensions: it writes them into <DATA_DIR>/agents/<harness>/skills and hands the directory over as AGENT_HUB_INSTALLED_SKILLS_DIR); the adapter only points its harness at that directory — pi/jouzu with `--no-skills --skill <dir>` (so the user's own skill directories stay out of a hub-managed session), dsh with DSH_AGENTS_HOME. It is reported PER SESSION, because a catalogue depends on the session's directory. Skills no longer ride config/set: one path, one source.

fork.note: pi/jouzu: fork at the next turn's first user message (their fork excludes the anchored message), or clone for the whole conversation; dsh: session.fork with atSeq snapped to the completed-turn boundary. The hub anchor is a turn, never a raw harness id.

stats.note: pi/jouzu: get_session_stats. dsh: the tokenUsage and contextPressure projections (plus sessionStats for the turn count). The hub also emits the same object as a `session.stats` event on the turn stream right after `turn.ended`, which is when the numbers move — there is no separate stats stream, because only dsh pushes projection updates and pi/jouzu push nothing.

compact.note: pi/jouzu: the native `compact` command (its response carries the result). dsh: the `/compact` command over commands/execute; the result names the compaction/summary event seq, from which the adapter reads the summary and the replaced-token count out of the session log. Both harnesses also report a compaction they performed on their own: the hub turns those into session.compacting / session.compacted on the turn stream, so a caller sees one shape whether it asked or not.

rename.note: pi/jouzu: set_session_name (the accepted name is read back from get_state, since the command itself answers only success). dsh: session.rename, which answers with the normalized title and the seq of the session/title event it appended. Refused (409 session_busy) while a turn is running, like every other PATCH knob.

runtime.rule: the plugin materialises the runtime its manifest pins (`runtime.package` + `runtime.version`) into `<plugin>/runtime`, the directory the manifest's command is relative to, and answers with what it did. The hub never installs a harness itself and knows nothing about packages: it asks, waits, and verifies the declared command now exists. A plugin that brings its own runtime does not declare this capability.
runtime.calledAutomatically: before startAdapter() when the runtime the manifest declares is not on disk yet, and again (idempotently) by POST /v1/hub/plugins/{id}/prepare

history-readonly.note: Native history is readable without starting an execution runtime.

checkedBy: the hub's boot self-check compares this file with the adapter requests it sends, the capabilities each manifest declares and the methods each adapter handles; a disagreement stops the hub before it serves anything
note: What an adapter says to its harness is its own dialect and deliberately NOT here: this file is only what the hub and an adapter say to each other. (deepseek listening to turn/start, assistant/chunk, tool/call, tool/result, turn/end, plan/mode is exactly that — its harness speaking, translated by the adapter into the events below.) A method or event the HUB sends or handles, or an adapter emits toward the hub, must be declared here.
